text: The Azure Line runs from Harbour Row to Dunmore Park, calling at Kestrel Green, Alder Vale, Brickworks, Copper Lane. It is operated with Series 400 four-car sets and carries an average weekday ridership of 73 thousand journeys. Headways are 5 minutes in the morning peak and 9 minutes in the evening off-peak.

The Crimson Line runs from Eastgate Quay to Jubilee Fields, calling at Foundry Bridge, Garnet Hill, Hollow Mill, Ironside. It is operated with Series 500 six-car sets and carries an average weekday ridership of 87 thousand journeys. Headways are 5 minutes in the morning peak and 9 minutes in the evening off-peak.

The Jade Line runs from Kingsmoor to Pennyford, calling at Larkspur, Mallow Street, Netherby, Oakhurst. The Amber Line runs from Quarry Side to Vantage Point, calling at Redcliff, Saltmarsh, Thistlebank, Underbank. The Violet Line runs from Westmere to Dovecote, calling at Yarrow Cross, Ashfen, Beacon Rise, Carrow End. The Slate Line runs from Elmsworth to Juniper Row, calling at Fallowfield, Glasshouse, Hartsmere, Ivory Dock. It is operated with Series 200 heritage sets and carries an average weekday ridership of 73 thousand journeys. Headways are 5 minutes in the morning peak and 9 minutes in the evening off-peak.

The TX-440 traction inverter is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is phase imbalance trip, which presents as unbalanced current draw across the three output phases. A TX-440 unit has a design life of 9 years and is classified as a safety-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group TX440G.

The HV-21 pantograph head is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is carbon strip fracture, which presents as a sudden loss of overhead contact force. A HV-21 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group HV21G.

The BR-7 regenerative brake unit is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is resistor grid overheat, which presents as grid temperature above the 310 degree cut-out. A BR-7 unit has a design life of 12 years and is classified as a safety-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group BR7G.

The PD-90 platform screen door controller is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is obstruction sensor drift, which presents as false obstruction reports on an empty threshold. A PD-90 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group PD90G.

The SG-12 signal interlocking relay is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is contact welding, which presents as a relay that fails to drop out after de-energising. A SG-12 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a safety-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group SG12G.

The AX-3 axle bearing assembly is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is thermal spike, which presents as a bearing temperature rise of more than 40 degrees in ten minutes. A AX-3 unit has a design life of 12 years and is classified as a safety-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group AX3G.

The CP-55 compressor module is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is pressure bleed-down, which presents as main reservoir pressure falling below 6.2 bar while stabled. A CP-55 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group CP55G.

The DR-8 door engine actuator is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is leadscrew backlash, which presents as a door leaf that rebounds before locking. A DR-8 unit has a design life of 12 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group DR8G.

The PS-19 auxiliary power supply is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is ripple fault, which presents as excess ripple voltage on the 110 volt battery bus. A PS-19 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group PS19G.

The TC-6 track circuit transmitter is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is frequency drift, which presents as a carrier frequency outside the 83 to 87 hertz window. A TC-6 unit has a design life of 12 years and is classified as a safety-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group TC6G.

The VE-31 tunnel ventilation fan is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is blade imbalance, which presents as vibration velocity above 7 millimetres per second at the bearing housing. A VE-31 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group VE31G.

The ES-14 escalator drive chain is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is elongation wear, which presents as chain elongation beyond the 1.5 percent service limit. A ES-14 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group ES14G.

The LT-77 lighting ballast is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is flicker cascade, which presents as a cascading flicker across an entire platform circuit. A LT-77 unit has a design life of 8 years and is classified as a service-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group LT77G.

The WS-5 wheel slide protection valve is fitted across the fleet and in fixed installations. Its dominant failure mode is latched release, which presents as a brake release that stays latched after the slide event clears. A WS-5 unit has a design life of 12 years and is classified as a safety-critical asset. Replacement units are held at the central store under part group WS5G.

Maintenance procedure MP-101: Inverter phase balance verification. Applies to the TX-440 traction inverter. Scheduled every 90 days. Method: apply the local isolation, measure against the acceptance table, replace any part outside limits, and seal the enclosure. Two competent staff are required and the work takes about 85 minutes.

Maintenance procedure MP-102: Inverter gate driver replacement. Applies to the TX-440 traction inverter. Scheduled on condition. Method: isolate the unit, record the as-found reading, carry out the corrective step, then prove the unit through two full cycles. Two competent staff are required and the work takes about 100 minutes. This procedure supersedes MP-101, which is withdrawn from the maintenance plan.

Service incident 2026/01 on 2026-01-04: trains were held at Harbour Row on the Azure Line for 11 minutes after a TX-440 traction inverter suffered a phase imbalance trip. 3 trains were held behind the failure and the station was placed in degraded mode until the unit was isolated. Customers were advised to use alternative routes.
